title: Water treatment P&ID symbol coverage
goal: An instrument engineer can read the process line from source to discharge and identify every tagged item.

rubric.must: No process or signal line passes through the inside of an equipment or instrument symbol.
Every process line carries an arrowhead showing flow direction.
Every instrument bubble's tag text fits inside the bubble and is readable.
Each equipment tag sits next to the item it names, with no ambiguity about which item it belongs to.
Instrument signal lines are visually distinct from process piping (dashed or thinner).
No two pieces of text overlap, and no text is crossed by a line.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex, which preferred its own SVG over the generated picture. Every tag, line and instrument in the source is present, with arrowheads on all piping. Reviewed and corrected: the dosing line's arrowhead sat on the filter's own outline, where it could not be seen.

audit.reviewedBy: a process engineer reviewing a P&ID before HAZOP

findings.what: The diaphragm dosing pump has no discharge overpressure protection or injection non-return valve.
findings.why: A blocked injection connection can overpressure the dosing line. Process pressure can also drive water backward into the chemical system.
findings.fix: Add a suitably rated relief valve returning to TK-201 and a non-return valve at the injection point; confirm any integral pump protection provides equivalent protection.

findings.what: The filter feed, backwash supply and drain are permanently connected without isolation valves.
findings.why: There is no defined filtration or backwash operating configuration. Water can escape to the sump or enter the backwash tank, and backwash cannot be directed reliably through the media.
findings.fix: Add isolation valves on the filter feed, chemical injection, backwash and drain connections. Use XV-101 for product isolation only if suitable, and define the valve positions for filtration, backwash and maintenance.

findings.what: FIC-101 commands XV-101 but receives no flow measurement.
findings.why: The flow controller cannot close its loop or regulate filtered-water flow without a measured input.
findings.fix: Add a tagged flow transmitter on the filtered-water line and connect its measurement signal to FIC-101.

findings.what: P-101 has no shown protection against a closed outlet or loss of suction water.
findings.why: Closing XV-101 can leave the transfer pump running at zero flow; emptying TK-101 can cause dry running and pump damage.
findings.fix: Add a TK-101 low-level pump trip and inhibit or stop P-101 when the discharge path is closed. Confirm the pump's minimum-flow requirement and provide protection if operation below it remains possible.

findings.what: The pumps cannot be isolated, and the filter has no shown high-point vent.
findings.why: Pump maintenance requires draining connected tanks or pipework. The filter cannot be reliably vented during filling or checked and relieved of trapped pressure before opening.
findings.fix: Add pump suction and discharge isolation valves and safe bleed points, plus a valved high-point vent on F-101; retain its drain with the isolation valve described above.
